title: Dashboards: standard SLO dashboard set per tier and per region + naming/ownership
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy
description:
Goal
Create a consistent, discoverable set of SLO + error budget dashboards for Hosted API and Dedicated tiers, standardized by region (and optionally model/route within cardinality limits). Document naming, folder structure, dashboard requirements, and ownership conventions so oncall + product can reliably find “the” SLO view.

Context
As part of tier-aware SLOs + error budgets, we need a canonical dashboard set that:
- is consistent across Hosted vs Dedicated
- supports region-level and tier-level drilldowns
- links directly to burn policy + runbooks
- works with the chosen SLI definitions (streaming TTFT vs stream duration, disconnect taxonomy, timeout classification)
- stays within metric cardinality budgets

Deliverables
1) Dashboard folder structure + naming convention (Grafana)
2) Standard dashboard templates (Hosted + Dedicated)
3) Required panels + variables + annotations (links, owners, runbooks)
4) Owner mapping and oncall routing info embedded in dashboards
5) Confluence doc describing the above (with screenshots) and “how to use” notes for oncall + Support

Proposed folder structure (Grafana)
Folder: SLO / Error Budgets
- Hosted API
  - Overview (All Regions)
  - Region: us-east-1
  - Region: us-west-2
  - Region: eu-west-1
- Dedicated
  - Overview (All Regions)
  - Region: us-east-1
  - Region: us-west-2
  - Region: eu-west-1

Naming conventions
Dashboards should follow:
- "SLO — <Tier> — <Region|All Regions>"
Examples:
- "SLO — Hosted — All Regions"
- "SLO — Hosted — us-east-1"
- "SLO — Dedicated — eu-west-1"

Panel requirements (minimum)
All dashboards MUST include:
- Error budget remaining (30d rolling) and burn rate (multi-window)
- Availability / success-rate SLI (per canonical SLI spec)
- 5xx rate (separate from success-rate if success includes partial classes)
- Timeout rate (gateway + upstream timeout where applicable)
- Streaming disconnect rate (Hosted only, and only for streaming routes)
- Latency SLIs:
  - Non-streaming: p95 and p99 end-to-end
  - Streaming: TTFT p95/p99 (primary) + stream duration p95/p99 (secondary)
- Volume context: request rate + token rate (or proxy) for interpreting burns
- Deploy/rollout overlay (from release events) + incident markers
- Links (top of dashboard):
  - Tiered SLO definitions (Confluence)
  - Error budget policy (Confluence)
  - Error budget exhaustion runbook
  - Primary owner (team + Slack channel)

Tier-specific requirements
Hosted
- Breakdowns by route group at minimum:
  - chat/completions streaming
  - chat/completions non-streaming
  - embeddings
- Optional (guarded by cardinality): top-N models by traffic for the selected region
- “Protective throttling” activation panel (if available) and a correlation view with error rate

Dedicated
- Must include “Dedicated pool readiness” SLI panel(s):
  - pool provision-to-ready
  - scheduler health + capacity signal (per Vanessa/Gabe spec)
- Drilldown by customer pool MUST be permissioned/restricted (no default broad access dashboards).
- For the standard region dashboards: aggregate across pools, with an optional filter for “pool_id” only in restricted folder.

Variables / filters (standard)
Required variables:
- tier (hosted|dedicated) [for shared templates]
- region
- route_group (hosted only)
Optional variables (only if cardinality budget allows):
- model_family (e.g., llama3, qwen2, mistral)
- model (guard: top-N only; never free-form high-cardinality)

Annotations / metadata
Each dashboard should have a standard header text block:
- Owner: <team> (Slack: #eng-sre, #eng-platform, etc.)
- Primary oncall rotation: <platform-oncall|dedicated-oncall>
- Data source: SLI metrics version (e.g., sli.v2)
- Last reviewed: date

Implementation plan
- Start from observability-pack templates (PR #77) and align on:
  - the final SLI metric names from ENG-2418/2419
  - the computed budget series emitted by ENG-2421
  - label/cardi constraints from ENG-2424
- Build Hosted dashboard first (us-east-1 pilot), validate with SRE oncall during a game-day.
- Replicate to remaining regions, then Dedicated.
- Write Confluence page with:
  - folder structure
  - naming
  - “how to interpret” notes for burn panels
  - link map to policy + runbooks

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Dashboards exist for Hosted and Dedicated: All Regions + each of (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1)
- [ ] Each dashboard includes the required panels + standardized variables
- [ ] Dashboards include top-of-page links to SLO definitions + error budget policy + runbooks
- [ ] Owner + oncall routing info is visible on each dashboard
- [ ] Dedicated customer/pool drilldowns are permissioned (restricted folder) and not broadly discoverable
- [ ] Dashboards have been validated against at least 48h of data (no empty panels, no obvious double-counting)
- [ ] Confluence page published documenting naming/folder/ownership (canonical reference)

Links
- Confluence (dashboard naming/structure): sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/slo-dashboards-structure-and-naming.json
- Error budget burn alerting standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/error-budget-burn-rate-alerting-standard.json
- Related PR: sources/github/observability-pack/pull_request_77.json

Open questions
- Do we want a single cross-tier “Executive Overview” dashboard (burn + availability only) or keep tier-separated to reduce confusion?
- For Hosted model drilldowns: do we standardize on model_family only to stay within label budgets, or allow top-5 models?
- Confirm standard region list for FY26 H1 (APAC region dashboards deferred unless usage warrants).

2026-02-10 — Aisha Bello: For Hosted streaming latency, make TTFT the primary SLI panel; stream duration should be present but clearly secondary. Also add disconnect taxonomy panel to distinguish client abort vs server fault (ties to ENG-2428).

2026-02-14 — Felix Schneider: Dedicated pool drilldowns must be in restricted folder. We should avoid even showing pool_id variable on the standard dashboard to prevent accidental leakage; use a separate “Dedicated (Restricted)” folder with tighter RBAC.

2026-02-18 — Sergio Costa: Implemented dashboard templates in observability-pack; added header blocks with owner + runbook links. Pending review of variable naming consistency with SLI toolkit (ENG-2421) and final metric names after 18433/18486 land.
